memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'I will grant peace in the land, and you will lie down and no one will
make you afraid. I will remove wild beasts from the land, and the sword
will not pass through your country'" - Lev 26:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Of all the blessings listed, this one touches something deep: you will
lie down and no one will make you afraid. Picture it — sleeping without
dread, resting without a knot of anxiety, lying down in genuine peace.

How many people cannot do that? They lie down and the worries crowd in.
The mind races through fears about money, health, family, the future.
Rest of body without rest of soul is no rest at all.

God promised Israel peace in their land as part of the national covenant.
While we should not claim these specific national promises as our own, the
peace God gives to His people is a thread that runs unbroken into the New
Covenant — and there it deepens.

Dear reader, the psalmist wrote, in peace I will lie down and sleep, for
you alone, LORD, make me dwell in safety (Ps 4:8). That peace was never
merely the absence of enemies; it was the presence of a trustworthy God.

Jesus said, peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. I do not give to
you as the world gives (John 14:27). Paul speaks of a peace that
transcends all understanding, guarding our hearts and minds (Phil 4:7).

This peace does not always remove the storm. It steadies us within it.
Even when the outward situation is unresolved, the soul anchored in
Christ can lie down and rest.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What keeps me from lying down in peace at night?
2. Is my peace based on circumstances or on trusting God?
3. What worry could I hand to God before I sleep tonight?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, so many fears steal my rest. Give me the peace that only You
provide, so that I can lie down and sleep, trusting myself into Your
hands. Amen.
